subject: math
title: Divide Unit Fractions and Whole Numbers
seo_title: Grade 5 Dividing Fractions Worksheets: Unit Fractions ÷ Whole Numbers, Whole Numbers ÷ Unit Fractions, Models and Word Problems
standard_text: Apply and extend previous understandings of division to divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions. Interpret division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number, and compute such quotients. Interpret division of a whole number by a unit fraction, and compute such quotients. Solve real world problems involving division of unit fractions by non-zero whole numbers and division of whole numbers by unit fractions.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 worksheets on dividing fractions: find how many 1/4s are in 3, share 1/2 into 3 equal parts, use fraction bars, area models and number lines, check with multiplication, and solve sharing and serving word problems. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: 3 ÷ 1/4 asks how many fourths are in 3. 1/2 ÷ 3 cuts 1/2 into 3 equal parts.
key_sub: 3 ÷ 1/4 = 12, because 12 × 1/4 = 3. 1/2 ÷ 3 = 1/6, because 1/6 × 3 = 1/2. Dividing by a unit fraction gives a bigger number; dividing a unit fraction by a whole number gives a smaller piece.
body_html:
The big idea: two kinds of division

In Grade 5 you divide with unit fractions (fractions with 1 on top) in two ways.

ProblemQuestion it asksAnswer
3 ÷ 14How many fourths are in 3?12 (bigger than 3)
12 ÷ 3Cut 12 into 3 equal parts. How big is each part?16 (smaller than 12)

Whole number ÷ unit fraction

Ask: how many of the unit fraction fit in the whole number? Each whole has 4 fourths, so 3 wholes have 3 × 4 = 12 fourths.

Example

How many 13-cup scoops are in 5 cups?

Each cup has 3 thirds. 5 × 3 = 15, so 5 ÷ 13 = 15.

Answer: 15 scoops

Unit fraction ÷ whole number

Cut the fraction into that many equal parts. Then ask: what fraction of the whole is one part?

Example

14 of a pizza is shared equally by 2 friends. How much of the pizza does each friend get?

Cut 14 into 2 equal parts. The whole pizza has 4 × 2 = 8 of these parts, so 14 ÷ 2 = 18.

Answer: 18 of the pizza

Check with multiplication

Multiply the answer by the number you divided by. You should get the number you started with.

DivisionCheck
13 ÷ 4 = 112112 × 4 = 412 = 13
4 ÷ 13 = 1212 × 13 = 123 = 4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
4 ÷ 13 = 43 (dividing 4 by 3)Count the thirds in 4: 4 × 3 = 12. The answer is bigger than 4.
13 ÷ 4 = 43 (multiplying)Cutting into parts makes them smaller: 112
13 ÷ 4 = 12 (mixing up the two kinds)12 is 4 ÷ 13. Here 13 is cut into 4 parts.
12 ÷ 3 = 13 (a part of the half)Compare with the whole: 6 parts make 1, so 16

faq.q: How do you divide a whole number by a unit fraction?
faq.a: Ask how many of the unit fraction fit in the whole number. 3 ÷ 1/4 = 12, because each whole has 4 fourths and 3 × 4 = 12.

faq.q: How do you divide a unit fraction by a whole number?
faq.a: Cut the fraction into that many equal parts and see what part of the whole each piece is. 1/2 ÷ 3 = 1/6, because 1/6 × 3 = 1/2.

faq.q: Why is the answer bigger when you divide by a fraction?
faq.a: Dividing by 1/2 asks how many halves fit, and every whole holds 2 halves. So 6 ÷ 1/2 = 12, which is greater than 6.
No. Standard 5.NF.B.7 covers only unit fractions and whole numbers, solved with models and a multiplication check. Dividing any fraction by any fraction comes in Grade 6 (6.NS.A.1).

items.q: Without finding the answer, 6 ÷ 12 is ___ 6.
items.e: Each whole holds 2 halves, so there are more halves than wholes. 6 ÷ 12 is greater than 6 (it is 12).

items.q: Without finding the answer, 5 ÷ 13 is ___ 5.
items.e: Each whole holds 3 thirds, so there are more thirds than wholes. 5 ÷ 13 is greater than 5 (it is 15).

items.q: Without finding the answer, 8 ÷ 14 is ___ 8.
items.e: Each whole holds 4 fourths, so there are more fourths than wholes. 8 ÷ 14 is greater than 8 (it is 32).

items.q: Without finding the answer, 14 ÷ 3 is ___ 14.
items.e: Cutting 14 into 3 equal parts makes each part smaller than 14. 14 ÷ 3 is less than 14 (it is 112).

items.q: Without finding the answer, 12 ÷ 5 is ___ 12.
items.e: Cutting 12 into 5 equal parts makes each part smaller than 12. 12 ÷ 5 is less than 12 (it is 110).

items.q: Without finding the answer, 16 ÷ 2 is ___ 16.
items.e: Cutting 16 into 2 equal parts makes each part smaller than 16. 16 ÷ 2 is less than 16 (it is 112).

items.q: Which is greater: 3 ÷ 12 or 12 ÷ 3?
items.e: 3 ÷ 12 = 6 and 12 ÷ 3 = 16. 6 is greater than 16.

items.q: Which is greater: 4 ÷ 16 or 4 ÷ 13?
items.e: 4 ÷ 16 = 24 and 4 ÷ 13 = 12. 24 is greater than 12. Sixths are smaller than thirds, so more of them fit in 4.

items.q: Which is greater: 13 ÷ 2 or 13 ÷ 4?
items.e: 13 ÷ 2 = 16 and 13 ÷ 4 = 112. 16 is greater than 112. Cutting into fewer parts makes bigger parts.

items.q: Which is greater: 2 ÷ 15 or 5 ÷ 12?
items.e: 2 ÷ 15 = 10 and 5 ÷ 12 = 10. Both are 10, so they are equal.

items.q: Which is greater: 12 ÷ 4 or 14 ÷ 2?
items.e: 12 ÷ 4 = 18 and 14 ÷ 2 = 18. Both are 18, so they are equal.

items.q: Sam says 13 ÷ 4 = 43. What did he do?
c: He divided by the bottom number only.
He mixed up the two kinds of division.
items.e: Sam found 13 × 4 = 43. Dividing 13 into 4 parts must give a smaller piece: 13 ÷ 4 = 112. Check: 112 × 4 = 412 = 13.
